# Limitations & Pain Points

Bundle size, styling conflicts, component gaps, and upgrade friction.
See [citations.md](../citations.md) for source details.

## Bundle Size

### Full Bundle (Bundlephobia)

| Metric | Size |
|--------|------|
| CSS (minified) | 2.17 MB [36] |
| CSS (gzipped) | 131 KB [36] |
| JS (minified) | 550 KB [36] |
| JS (gzipped) | 151 KB [36] |
| Dependencies | 6 [36] |
| Largest dependency | @patternfly/react-styles (~1.52 MB) [36] |

Combined gzipped payload: ~282 KB (Calculated: 131 KB CSS + 151 KB JS) [36].

### Comparison (application-level)

A Cockpit starter-kit migration from PatternFly React to PatternFly Elements
(Lit web components) showed [34]:
- Compressed JS: 80 kB → 29 kB (64% reduction)
- CSS: 23 kB → 0 kB (eliminated with web components)
- node_modules: 381 MB → 202 MB (47% reduction)

## PF5 → PF6 Migration Friction

### CSS Variable Renaming

All CSS variables renamed with no automatic mapping [3]:
- `--pf-v5-global--FontSize--lg` → `--pf-t--global--font--size--lg`
- React tokens: `global_FontSize_lg` → `t_global_font_size_lg`
- "Some changes will still require manual intervention" [3]
- Undefined tokens marked with hot pink by the tokens-update codemod [3]

### Breakpoint Unit Change

Breakpoints converted from px to rem, requiring updates wherever breakpoint
values are referenced [3]:

| Breakpoint | Previous | New |
|-----------|----------|-----|
| sm | 576px | 36rem |
| md | 768px | 48rem |
| lg | 992px | 62rem |
| xl | 1200px | 75rem |
| 2xl | 1450px | 90.625rem |

### Component Deprecations and Renames

- Chip → Label [3][16]
- Tile → Card [3][16]
- Text → Content [3][16]
- Expandable Section → `isActive` prop removed [3]
- Empty State → significant refactoring required [3]

### Chart Library Changes

Victory-based charts moved to new import path (`@patternfly/react-charts/victory`)
and Victory became an optional peer dependency [3]. Apache ECharts added as an
alternative in 6.2 [4].

### Test Failures

Known test breakage patterns [3]:
- **Button:** `aria-disabled` behavior changed; use `byRole` instead of `byText`
- **Select:** menu options inaccessible in tests; pass `{hidden: true}` or use
  `appendTo: "inline"`

### Migration Tooling

66 ESLint-based codemods help automate the migration [17]:
- `class-name-updater` — pf-v5 → pf-v6 prefixes
- `tokens-update` — React tokens + global CSS vars
- `css-vars-updater` — non-React files (.css, .scss, .md)

"Added around 30 additional codemods" between alpha and beta [17]. Manual
intervention still required for complex cases [3].

## PatternFly Elements Component Gaps

PatternFly Elements (Lit-based web components) has "still a lot of components
missing compared to PatternFly React" — including Alert, Checkbox, TimePicker [34].

Additional pain points [34]:
- Shadow DOM breaks standard DOM querying in tests — required
  `query-selector-shadow-dom` module
- `npm new` produced broken TypeScript code
- Missing Alert component required recovery from an abandoned PR

## Dark Theme Limitations

- Charts require separate CSS import (`@patternfly/patternfly/patternfly-charts.css`) [7]
- Images require manual handling (4 approaches: inline SVG, universal colors,
  container, CSS swapping) — they do not automatically adapt [7]
- High contrast mode is beta as of 6.4.0 [6]
- Palette tokens must never be used directly in production code [6][8]

## Accessibility Gaps

- PatternFly.org website scorecard (November 2024): 133 violations remaining,
  0% critical/major resolved [10]
- CI/CD accessibility integration was partial [10]
- Testing guide acknowledges it "will not cover every scenario" [14]
- No formal VPAT published

## Missing Features

- No React Server Components (RSC) support documented [41][42]
- Next.js compatibility has documented issues (historical — SSR, build performance) [42]
- No React Compiler compatibility information found
- No formal governance document (GOVERNANCE.md) [13]

## Gaps and Limitations of This Analysis

- No community survey or developer satisfaction data on PF5→PF6 migration effort
- Bundle size figures are full-package; real-world tree-shaken sizes vary by usage
- PatternFly Elements data comes from a single third-party blog post [34]
- No formal migration effort estimates (hours/days) found in any source
